clue.text: Crackling in exaltation, having left the City

indicators.note: having left says a piece walks out of the longer word

parts.note: a state of exaltation is an ecstatic one, rapture
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to escape London finds their joy fizzing like a bad radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' takes EC out of ECSTATIC; the City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical interference heard as crackling on a radio is called static.

clue.text: Trade cuts out sad flowers

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Job losses in trade leave people sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' are things that flow: tear ducts flow when sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear ducts make tears flow when one is sad, so they are sad things that flow.

clue.text: Finished clue for "E"

definitions.meaning: E is the last letter of the word the, its final letter

explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it is at its conclusion, and E is the closing letter of 'the'.

clue.text: Restaurant music finale: celebration in song

indicators.note: finale means the last letter of the word
in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
a fete is a celebration or festival

explanation.surface: A restaurant's grand finish: a party in song.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant.

clue.text: On a ship overseas subject to right promotion

indicators.note: promotion moves the letter for right to a new place in the word

parts.note: living overseas means living abroad

explanation.surface: A sailor abroad hopes to be promoted for doing the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to ... promotion' shifts the R of ABROAD two places along, giving ABOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard means being on a vessel, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Crime of boy on a rooftop

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the boy below the earlier letters

parts.note: the top of the word roof is R
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy climbing a roof commits a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of setting fire to property.

clue.text: Clear river akin to 18 12

parts.note: overt means open or clear
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A clear river just like half an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 12 here is read as the 1812 Overture, a well-known overture.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1812 is an overture, so an overture is a work of the same kind.

clue.text: One for love in wireless spokes

indicators.note: for means one letter replaces another

parts.note: wireless is an old word for radio
love is zero in tennis, so O
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone falls in love with a voice on the wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii are the spokes of a circle, lines from centre to rim.

clue.text: One might 18 12, amazing feat involving beer

indicators.note: involving means one piece is wrapped around another
amazing suggests the letters of feat are thrown into disarray

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A remarkable stunt pulled off with a pint in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' scrambles the feat, and 'involving' wraps it round the beer. 18 12 is HALF-INCH, Cockney rhyming slang for pinch (steal); TEA LEAF is rhyming slang for thief.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a thief is a tea leaf, someone who would pinch things.

clue.text: 18 12 6 writer starting to compose short poem broadcaster heard of first

indicators.note: first places the spoken word ahead of the broadcaster
starting takes the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: a haiku is a short poem, cut short here by one letter

indicators.note: heard means the word is given as it is pronounced

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like OV
Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: Instructions for writing a short poem for broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 12 6 is the 1812 Overture; 'of' is pronounced OV.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky composed the 1812 Overture, so he is its writer.

clue.text: Slight one who'd be profligate with a penny for a pound

indicators.note: for here means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: a profligate person is a big spender
P is the abbreviation for a penny
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A slight figure is wasteful, swapping pennies for pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: SPENDER has its P (penny) swapped for L (pound).
explanation.definitionFit: Slight and slender both describe a thin, delicate build.

clue.text: Really gutted, having eaten bird, no longer hungry, alas

indicators.note: having eaten means the outer letters swallow the others
gutted means the inside of the word is removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: an egret is a kind of heron
after eating you are full

explanation.surface: Someone is upset after eating a bird and being full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' keeps only the outer letters of Really; 'having eaten' puts the bird and the full feeling inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Regretfully, like alas, expresses sorrow.

clue.text: Out of sight tonight, no possibility of wild goose chase

parts.note: someone out of sight is in hiding

indicators.note: possibility of signals one possible rearrangement of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone vanishing tonight makes a search pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a hiding to nothing' is a British idiom for an effort that cannot succeed; 'possibility of' signals one possible arrangement of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A futile pursuit with no chance of success is like being on a hiding to nothing, an idiom for doomed effort.

clue.text: See 18
Trivial about one role in three

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: trite means banal or trivial
a part is a role in a play
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a minor role as one of three.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripartite describes something divided into or made of three parts.

clue.text: Cards shuffled or he's one with a load

parts.note: a pack is a set of playing cards

indicators.note: shuffled means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dealer shuffles cards for someone weighed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A packhorse is an animal used to carry loads.

clue.text: At home having a ball around five — that's early

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: around means one piece goes round another

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone at home throws a ball for five people, ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in advance means doing it early.

clue.text: Not wild or forced entry

definitions.meaning: a horse that is tamed is no longer wild

explanation.definitionFit: A horse that has been tamed is broken in, and a burglar who has smashed a door has broken in.

clue.text: Keeping page almost at start of chapter in honour

indicators.note: in means these letters sit inside the honour

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a page is a young servant

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A page, kept at the start of a chapter, is honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts SERVANT to SERVAN; add C from 'start of chapter' and put the lot 'in' OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Observance of a rule means keeping it, as in keeping the Sabbath.

clue.text: Appropriate short distance

definitions.meaning: to appropriate is to pinch, for which ... is Cockney rhyming slang

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it: half-inch, pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses half-inch for pinch, meaning steal, and literally it is a small measurement.

clue.text: Cockney tried to let one in at a leisurely pace

indicators.note: to let in means one piece is admitted inside another
in completes the phrase to let in, an insertion

parts.note: a Cockney drops the h, so had a go becomes 'ad a go
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Londoner tried letting someone in, slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop the H, so 'had a go' (tried) becomes 'AD A GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a slow tempo.

clue.text: The very one, she'd accepted climax frequently sinful

indicators.note: accepted means one piece takes the others inside it

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
a peak is a climax
oft is an old word for often
evil means wicked or sinful

explanation.surface: She frequently gave in to wicked pleasure at the height of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' puts the climax and frequently pieces inside she'd; the clue's apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when the person just being discussed appears, the very one we meant.

clue.text: Spot on skirt's first to go in intercourse

indicators.note: to go means the letter is removed

parts.note: intercourse is the sex act

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of skirt

explanation.surface: A skirt comes off for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise, spot on.

clue.text: Sweet cheat

explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft confection, and to fudge results is to fiddle them dishonestly.

clue.text: Desired study reversed after a long time

indicators.note: after places the study piece behind the long time

parts.note: a year can stand for a long time

indicators.note: reversed means the word for study is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Someone longed for their study back after years away.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for or desire something.

clue.text: The ultimate in domestic energy distribution for 18 11 to 20

indicators.note: distribution means the letters are spread out and rearranged
the ultimate in means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A final word on how home energy is shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: C (the last of 'domestic') joins ENERGY and is rearranged. 18 11 to 20 reads as 1811 to 1820, the years of the British Regency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Regency in Britain was the period from 1811 to 1820 when the Prince Regent ruled.

clue.text: Oldest ancestor's position

indicators.note: the 's reads as has, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: An ancestor's place in the family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a posture or position, physical or on an issue.

clue.text: Bananas ordered right away and eaten

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild
right away means the letter for right is removed

explanation.surface: Bananas were ordered at once and eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' takes an R from ORDERED, leaving ODERED, which 'Bananas' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroded means worn or eaten away, as by water.
